purpose: Measure the new research branch against actual main and a semantically equivalent Rust workload; identify remaining incremental compilation latency.

contrasts.main_new_B: Actual main binary with existing caches vs candidate --producer-reuse, graph disabled. This is the total branch effect, not attribution solely to the current continuation.
contrasts.new_A_B_C: A candidate existing caches, B shared producer plus materializer receipts, C B plus reactive graph; internal feature attribution only.
contrasts.Rust: Same arithmetic and call graph, edits and binary output oracle. Cargo check and opt-level2 build with incremental=true/codegen-units1/jobs1. Resident Zil request vs fresh Cargo process is explicitly a workflow comparison, not identical compiler phases.

rules: Hypothetical weights are sensitivity calculations, not measured user request frequencies.
Profiled diagnostics and unprofiled full request measurements remain separate.
Every edited request starts from a validated named parent; preserve all preparation rows.
All successful requests execute current independent Verify; O2 runs validate complete native outcomes.
No increased limits, changed cache policy, reduced optimization or source replacement.
Single-block and cross-window cost differences diagnose mechanisms, not accepted speedup.
Retain failed runs; report cold/broad/error/fallback separately from incremental edits.
Require actual shared Core/maps, sparse materializer walks and unchanged CFG recomputation before performance claims.
Revised before formal measurements per explicit user steering: compare main and Rust, not another active research branch.
main already has resident, function, analysis, semantic and object caches; do not describe it as an uncached baseline.
main lacks optional research counters/profile fields; validate its actual public report and current Verify without inventing work data.
Rust language checks are not equivalent to Zil independent Verify. Cross-language ratios do not prove equivalent assurance or code quality.
Rust and Zil measurements from separate windows are descriptive distributions, not matched-block causal confidence intervals.
